subject: Sizing and tenanting tradeoffs for MediSure pilot (Dedicated vs Private)
messages:

Cc: procurement@medisure.com
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Initial sizing request for regulated pilot

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week. MediSure is moving a pilot of our clinical summarization feature into a limited production environment and we need help sizing the inference footprint and understanding the hosting tradeoffs for a regulated workload. High level:
- Expected steady-state: ~25 req/s (concurrent user base across our SaaS front-end) with 1.2k token avg response; burst up to 120 req/s for short windows (10–15 minutes) during nightly processing.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for interactive flows.
- Compliance: SOC2 + regionally isolated tenancy required; some customers will require VPC-only or on-prem options.

Can you provide a short options matrix comparing: Dedicated reserved capacity vs Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for both pilot and full rollout? We need: rough GPU counts/types, expected throughput per GPU for our traffic profile, cold-start / cache considerations, and an estimate of timeline + procurement dependencies.

Attached is a quick traffic snapshot from our analytics team. We want a two-page summary and a recommended path (pilot->scale) for our procurement committee by May 6.

Thanks,
Liam

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Looping in some quick compute estimates and risks for the pilot. Notes based on Liam's numbers and our recent kernel perf tests for Llama2-70B-ish family (quantized mixed int8/16):

Assumptions: 1. baseline model = 16–24k context with a ~1.2k response average; 2. ~50% request token generation vs prompt tokens (rough).

Provisional sizing (pilot, conservative):
- Dedicated reserved pool approach (fastest time-to-launch): 3x H100-80GB (or 8x A100-80GB equivalents depending on availability) behind a single isolated tenant. Expected steady throughput per H100: ~8–12 req/s at p95 < 350ms with batching turned conservative for latency. Burst headroom via autoscale/burst nodes (on-demand) to handle the 120 req/s spikes.
- Private (VPC-hosted or on-prem appliance): For strict isolation + on-prem: estimate 4x H100-80GB to meet the same SLOs accounting for less autoscaling flexibility, plus network egress/design lead time. On-prem adds procurement lead times (hardware + rack) of 8–12 weeks vs Dedicated 2–4 weeks.

Key tradeoffs:
- Cost: Dedicated (reserved) is cheaper short-term and allows faster provisioning. Private has a higher fixed cost and longer procurement timeline but gives stronger network isolation for regulated customers.
- Risk: Private/on-prem increases ops surface area (support contracts, hardware refresh cadence). Dedicated with strict tenancy + CMK covers many compliance asks faster.

I'll draft a one-pager with these numbers and two scaled options (pilot and scale) — ping me if we should size with additional cache layers (prefix/KV) for hot-calls, which can significantly reduce GPU counts in steady-state.

— Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Hi all — I ran a short simulator on the attached traffic and sketched a recommended conservative plan we can present to procurement. Paste of the mini-summary below so it's inline in the thread: 

Option A — Dedicated (recommended for pilot):
- Pilot footprint: 3x H100-80GB dedicated (isolated tenant), autoscale policy to add up to +2 on short bursts. Expected p95 latency 250–320ms for interactive flows.
- Why: fastest procurement (2–4 weeks), lower initial CAPEX for MediSure, supports CMK integration, and we can gate-run SOC2 evidence in parallel.

Option B — Redwood Private (VPC + optional on-prem):
- Pilot footprint: 4x H100-80GB (or equivalent A100 mix). On-prem variant: add procurement lead 8–12 weeks and minimum rack/ops overhead.
- Why: ideal if MediSure requires full air-gapped on-prem for specific customers; higher TCO and longer lead time.

Fallbacks and mitigations:
- Cache hot prompts (KV/prefix) to lower average per-request GPU time (could reduce steady GPUs by ~25–40% depending on hit rate).
- Canary path: start pilot on Dedicated with strict tenancy + CMK; after SOC2 evidence and procurement signoff, migrate sensitive customers to Private/on-prem if required.

Action items for May 6 procurement deck:
- Ava: attach our one-pager options matrix (will finish by 04/28).
- Vivek: final GPU recommendation and autoscale settings for the pilot (ETA 04/26).
- MediSure: confirm KMS requirement and any minimum audit gating.

I'll prepare the numbers with conservative cost estimates and a timeline slide.

— Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect, Enterprise Inference
Redwood Inference
